added_failures_note: the reviewed manifest declares baseline_suite and after_suite absent, so I ran the gate myself at the base revision (660b2e36: 9 passed, EXIT=0) and at the reviewed head (6a411e5b, clean extraction: ten cases). Across 27 head runs 5 failed, every one the same added case, so added_failure_count 1 names an intermittent failure the base cannot have and the run's single reported run missed.

findings.text: blocking: the added rate-limit case test_two_crossing_passes_within_the_bound_write_one_snapshot fails intermittently. In my runs of the reviewed head (6a411e5b, clean git-archive extraction) 5 of 27 full-file runs failed with '1 failed, 9 passed', always this case, while the base revision 660b2e36 passed 9 of 9. FLEET_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL=3 with FLEET_SLEEP_SECONDS=2 leaves a one-second margin and bin/fleet-health rate-limits on second-resolution date +%s, so loop overhead plus second-boundary rounding lets the second pass cross the bound and write a second snapshot, failing 'assert len(box.snapshots()) == 1' with 'assert 2 == 1'. The run's manifest and fragment report 10 passed EXIT=0 from a single run and do not observe it, so the gate the section rests on is not reproducible.

follow-on: test_a_pass_after_the_bound_writes_a_second_snapshot is built the same way (interval 3, sleep 2, three passes) and asserts exactly 2 snapshots; the same timing margin can make the middle pass cross the bound and write a third, so it carries the identical flake hazard even though it passed in all of my runs.

follow-on: the module docstring still states 'Every case drives exactly one sampling pass (--once) against fixture readings', which the added cases falsify: two cases drive two and three passes through --passes, so the stated invariant no longer holds for the file.

follow-on: the second half of the prior review's file-hygiene follow-on is unfixed: tests/test_fleet_health.py still ends without a trailing newline at head (last byte 0x32), while commit 2a500dca8 restored only bin/fleet-health's newline (last byte 0x0a).

item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed range (commits 2a500dca8 and 6a411e5b) exists to close the prior review's two follow-ons; bin/fleet-health gains --passes and FLEET_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL/FLEET_SLEEP_SECONDS overrides and tests/test_fleet_health.py gains two multi-pass rate-limit cases, but tests/test_fleet_health.py keeps its missing trailing newline and its docstring keeps the one-pass claim the new cases break.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records base 3befbf4f0e, head 6a411e5b, gate '10 passed EXIT=0' and negative control '4 failed EXIT=1', and declares baseline_suite/after_suite absent. Its test_logs cite gate-head.log, whose header names rev 660b2e3660 but whose body collected 10 items, where 660b2e36's committed tests file collects only 9: the cited log was produced in a working tree carrying the uncommitted new cases and does not evidence the head revision it is cited for.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares bin/fleet-health, tests/test_fleet_health.py and the node's evidence fragment; git diff --stat 660b2e36..6a411e5b lists exactly those three and nothing else.

justifications.durability: the range adds a test whose assertion cannot hold reliably: the rate-limit case depends on second-resolution timing and 5 of 27 head runs failed on it, so the guard it was added to provide passes only sometimes and the gate fails open on the runs it happens to pass.
justifications.evidence: the gate is flaky at the reviewed head (5 of 27 runs failed, 1 failed 9 passed, clean extraction), and the run's own gate-head.log names rev 660b2e3660 while collecting 10 items, a revision whose committed tests file collects 9, so the log cited as the head-arm log does not evidence the head. The base arm (660b2e36) I ran reads 9 passed EXIT=0.
justifications.fit: the env-override idiom and the tests' sandbox fixture style are followed, but the module docstring is left stating a one-pass-per-case rule the new cases break, and bin/fleet-health now carries a --passes flag whose only caller is its own test file.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the additions are on-goal for the section and target the prior rate-limit follow-on, but that follow-on is only partly closed: the tests-file trailing newline remains unfixed and one added case does not pass reliably, so the range does not leave the section's gate dependable.
justifications.reuse: the additions reuse the existing FLEET_* env-override idiom and the script's own rate-limit mechanism rather than adding a parallel one, and introduce no new production call site; the only new caller is the test module.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 660b2e36..6a411e5b lists only bin/fleet-health, tests/test_fleet_health.py and the node's evidence fragment, all inside the manifest's declared write paths; no figure was written because the done-when names none.
